module.title: Then vs Now: Comparing Eras with 'Used To'
module.group: A2.3 - World Explorations, Stories & Bridge to B1
module.objective: Compare past eras with modern life, highlighting discontinued habits using 'used to' and 'didn't use to'.

subModules.title: Reading Mission: Then vs Now
subModules.grammarFocus: used to, didn't use to, did you use to

content.summary: Welcome to this reading mission about how daily life has changed over the years. In this module, you will read short texts comparing the past and the present. You will learn how to use 'used to' to talk about past habits that are different today.

linguisticTarget.grammar: Affirmative, negative, and question forms of 'used to' for past states and habits.
linguisticTarget.vocabulary: Words related to lifestyle, communication, technology, and childhood.
linguisticTarget.readingStrategy: Skimming paragraphs for general ideas and scanning for specific comparison details.

learningObjectives: Understand the main idea of short A2 texts about past and present lifestyles.
Locate specific details such as past communication methods and childhood games.
Recognize and practice grammar patterns with 'used to' and 'didn't use to'.

contextWarmup.prompt: How did people usually talk to their friends who lived far away thirty years ago?
options: They used to write letters and use landline phones.
They used to send instant messages on smartphones.
They used to send emails through high-speed internet.
contextWarmup.explanation: Thirty years ago, smartphones and high-speed internet were not common. People wrote letters on paper and called each other on landline phones.

rules: Use 'used to' plus the base form of a verb for habits or states that were true in the past but have changed now.
In negative sentences, use 'didn't use to' plus the base form. Notice that 'used' loses the letter d after 'did'.
In questions, start with 'Did', followed by the subject and 'use to' plus the base verb.

commonTrap.trapTitle: Using 'used to' for present habits or one-time actions
commonTrap.explanation: Learners often use 'used to' for things happening right now or for a single action in the past.
commonTrap.wrong: I use to wake up early every day now.
commonTrap.correct: Use the present simple for current habits: I wake up early every day now.

grammarFormulas.title: Sentence Patterns with Used To
grammarFormulas.description: Assemble sentence blocks to practice affirmative, negative, and question forms:

items.exampleSentence: I used to have a habit of biting my nails when I was younger.
items.collocation: I used to have a habit of...

items.exampleSentence: During my childhood, I used to visit my grandparents every weekend.
People used to send handwritten letters before email became popular.
We didn't use to have instant messengers like WhatsApp 20 years ago.
In the old era, children used to play more outdoor games.
Did you use to be afraid of technology when it first came out?
My grandmother's lifestyle used to be very different from mine.
People didn't use to have the convenience of online shopping.
Communication used to take days through postal mail.
The older generation used to spend more time talking face-to-face.

paragraphs: Life has changed a lot over the last fifty years. During my grandparents' childhood, the lifestyle was much simpler. Families did not use to have computers or smartphones. Instead, children used to spend their free time playing outdoor games in the street. Communication was also very different because people wrote handwritten letters and waited days for a reply.

Today, modern technology gives us incredible convenience. We can talk to friends instantly using messaging apps and video calls. People did not use to have this speed in the past. However, older generations often remember the old era with great fondness, because neighbors used to talk face-to-face every single day without screens distracting them.

The infinitive marker to sounds like ta in rapid conversation.
The consonants t and d merge into a ch sound.

subModules.title: Writing Mission: Comparing Past Habits with Used To

content.summary: Learn how to write clear sentences about past habits using used to, didn't use to, and did you use to.

blueprintItems.title: Step 1: Affirmative Sentences
blueprintItems.example: I used to play outside every day.

blueprintItems.title: Step 2: Negative Sentences
blueprintItems.formula: Subject + didn't use to + verb (base form)
blueprintItems.example: She didn't use to like vegetables.

blueprintItems.title: Step 3: Question Sentences
blueprintItems.formula: Did + subject + use to + verb (base form)?
blueprintItems.example: Did you use to watch cartoons?

mechanicsRules.rule: Remember to drop the letter d in use to when writing negative sentences and questions with did.
mechanicsRules.badExample: He didn't used to play tennis.
mechanicsRules.goodExample: He didn't use to play tennis.
mechanicsRules.why: When you use didn't or did, the main verb is use to without the letter d.

mechanicsRules.rule: Always start a sentence with a capital letter and end with a full stop.
mechanicsRules.badExample: i used to live in london.
mechanicsRules.goodExample: I used to live in London.
mechanicsRules.why: Every sentence needs a capital letter at the start, and proper nouns like London need capitals too.

mechanicsRules.rule: Use used to only for past habits that are finished, not for things happening now.
mechanicsRules.badExample: I used to play tennis every day now.
mechanicsRules.goodExample: I used to play tennis every day when I was young.
mechanicsRules.why: Used to describes past routines that changed, so it does not combine with words like now.

sampleSentences.en: I used to ride my bicycle to school when I was ten.
sampleSentences.id: Dulu saya biasa mengendarai sepeda ke sekolah ketika berumur sepuluh tahun.

sampleSentences.en: My brother didn't use to eat vegetables as a child.
sampleSentences.id: Saudara laki-laki saya dulu tidak suka makan sayur waktu kecil.

sampleSentences.en: Did your grandparents use to live in a small village?
sampleSentences.id: Apakah kakek nenekmu dulu tinggal di sebuah desa kecil?

sampleSentences.en: People used to write letters before mobile phones existed.
sampleSentences.id: Orang-orang dulu menulis surat sebelum ponsel ada.

mechanicsChallenges.targetSentence: Mark didn't use to play football on Sundays.
mechanicsChallenges.translation: Mark dulu tidak biasa bermain sepak bola pada hari Minggu.
mechanicsChallenges.keyRule: Use an apostrophe in didn't, use use to without d, and capitalize proper names and days.

mechanicsChallenges.faultySentence: did sara use to read books in the evening
mechanicsChallenges.targetSentence: Did Sara use to read books in the evening?
mechanicsChallenges.translation: Apakah Sara dulu biasa membaca buku di malam hari?
mechanicsChallenges.keyRule: Start questions with a capital letter, capitalize proper names, use use to, and end with a question mark.

mechanicsChallenges.faultySentence: we used to live in paris ten years ago
mechanicsChallenges.targetSentence: We used to live in Paris ten years ago.
mechanicsChallenges.translation: Kami dulu tinggal di Paris sepuluh tahun lalu.
mechanicsChallenges.keyRule: Capitalize the beginning of the sentence and proper city names like Paris.

guidedLabChallenges.title: Challenge 1: Describe Your Childhood Toys
guidedLabChallenges.instruction: Write three sentences about toys or games you played with when you were young. Use used to and didn't use to.
guidedLabChallenges.example: I used to play with wooden blocks every day. My sister used to have a favorite teddy bear. We didn't use to play video games.

guidedLabChallenges.title: Challenge 2: Then vs Now Life
guidedLabChallenges.instruction: Write three sentences comparing life in the past with life today. Mention how people communicated or traveled.
guidedLabChallenges.example: People used to send handwritten letters to friends. They didn't use to have smartphones. Now everyone uses fast internet.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Change the affirmative sentence into a negative sentence using didn't use to:
practicumQuestions.promptText: Tom used to eat vegetables when he was young.
practicumQuestions.hint: Use didn't use to instead of used to.
targetAnswers: Tom didn't use to eat vegetables when he was young.
practicumQuestions.explanation: In negative sentences, use didn't use to without the final letter d on use.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Change the statement into a question starting with Did:
practicumQuestions.promptText: You used to walk to school.
practicumQuestions.hint: Start with Did, use use to, and end with a question mark.
targetAnswers: Did you use to walk to school?
practicumQuestions.explanation: Questions start with Did, followed by the subject and use to without the letter d.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Combine these two ideas using because:
practicumQuestions.promptText: I stayed inside. It used to rain a lot in winter.
practicumQuestions.hint: Put the main action first and the reason after because.
targetAnswers: I stayed inside because it used to rain a lot in winter.
I stayed inside because it used to rain a lot during winter.
practicumQuestions.explanation: Use because to connect the action with the reason using past habit structures.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Fix the capitalisation and punctuation in this sentence:
practicumQuestions.promptText: did anna use to live in madrid
practicumQuestions.hint: Capitalize names and cities, and add a question mark.
targetAnswers: Did Anna use to live in Madrid?
practicumQuestions.explanation: Proper names like Anna and Madrid need capital letters, and questions need a question mark at the end.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Complete the sentence with the correct form of used to:
practicumQuestions.promptText: When I was seven, I _____ play piano every afternoon.
practicumQuestions.hint: Use the affirmative past habit form.
practicumQuestions.explanation: For past routines in an affirmative sentence, use used to before the base verb.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Change this negative sentence into an affirmative sentence:
practicumQuestions.promptText: They didn't use to watch TV on weekdays.
practicumQuestions.hint: Change didn't use to to used to.
targetAnswers: They used to watch TV on weekdays.
practicumQuestions.explanation: Change didn't use to to used_to for affirmative past habits.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Combine the clauses with but:
practicumQuestions.promptText: I used to love milk. I don't drink it now.
practicumQuestions.hint: Use a comma before but to show contrast.
targetAnswers: I used to love milk, but I don't drink it now.
I used to love milk, but I do not drink it now.
practicumQuestions.explanation: Use but to show contrast between past habits and present situations.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Fix the error with use to in this sentence:
practicumQuestions.promptText: My parents didn't used to have a car.
practicumQuestions.hint: Remove the d from used after didn't.
targetAnswers: My parents didn't use to have a car.
practicumQuestions.explanation: After didn't, the correct form is use to without the final d.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Fill in the blank with the correct question word:
practicumQuestions.promptText: _____ did your family use to spend summer holidays?
practicumQuestions.hint: Ask about a place or location.
practicumQuestions.explanation: Where asks about a location or place where past holidays happened.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Turn this sentence into a question:
practicumQuestions.promptText: Sarah used to have long hair.
practicumQuestions.hint: Start with Did and change used to to use to.
targetAnswers: Did Sarah use to have long hair?
practicumQuestions.explanation: To form a question in the past, place Did at the beginning and change used to to use to.

subModules.title: Speaking Lab: Comparing Eras with Used To

content.summary: Master the pronunciation of used to, where the final d links smoothly to to, sounding like /juːstə/. Practice clear vowel sounds and sentence stress when comparing past habits with present lifestyles.
content.audioGuidance: Pay attention to how the auxiliary verb didn't use to is pronounced as /dɪdnt ˈjuːstə/. Keep your intonation steady when listing past routines.

pillars.name: Linking Sounds
pillars.explanation: The d in used and the t in to blend together in spoken English.

pillars.name: Sentence Stress
pillars.explanation: Stress words like then, now, used to, and never to make your comparisons clear.

stressPairs.shiftExplanation: Notice that the primary stress remains on the first word in both affirmative and negative forms.
Observe the different syllable stress patterns between compound nouns and multi-syllable nouns.
Longer words shift primary stress towards the second half of the word.
Notice that compound nouns stress the first part, while abstract nouns often stress the middle syllable.

drills.targetText: I used to play outside with my friends every afternoon.
drills.phonetic: /aɪ ˈjuːstə pleɪ aʊtˌsaɪd wɪð maɪ frɛndz ˈɛvri ˈɑːftənuːn/
drills.focus: Pronunciation of used to and linking vowels
drills.hint: Blend used and to smoothly as /juːstə/.

drills.targetText: People didn't use to have smartphones twenty years ago.
drills.phonetic: /ˈpiːpl ˈdɪdnt ˈjuːstə hæv ˈsmɑːtˌfəʊnz ˈtwɛnti jɪəz əˈɡəʊ/
drills.focus: Negative form didn't use to and sentence rhythm
drills.hint: Keep use without a final d in the negative form.

drills.targetText: Did you use to read handwritten letters during your childhood?
drills.phonetic: /dɪd juː ˈjuːstə riːd ˈhændˌrɪtn ˈlɛtəz ˈdjʊərɪŋ jɔː ˈʧaɪldhʊd/
drills.focus: Question formation with did you use to
drills.hint: Raise your pitch slightly at the end of the question.

drills.targetText: My grandmother used to write letters before email existed.
drills.phonetic: /maɪ ˈɡrændˌmʌðə ˈjuːstə raɪt ˈlɛtəz bɪˈfɔːr ˈiːmeɪl ɪɡˈzɪstɪd/
drills.hint: Pause slightly between the main clause and the time clause.
